# EHDS Policy Page — Cached Snapshot

Source: https://health.ec.europa.eu/ehealth-digital-health-and-care/european-health-data-space_en
Snapshot date: 2026-08-19

## What the EHDS Regulation is about

The European Health Data Space (EHDS) is the first common EU data space dedicated to a specific sector. The EHDS Regulation establishes a common framework for the use and exchange of electronic health data across the EU. It:

1. empowers individuals to access, control and share their electronic health data across borders for healthcare delivery (**primary use**);
2. enables secure and trustworthy reuse of health data for research, innovation, policy-making, and regulatory activities (**secondary use**);
3. fosters a single market for electronic health record (EHR) systems, supporting both primary and secondary use.

## Publication and entry into force

- Officially published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 2025/327) on **5 March 2025**.
- **Enters into force on 26 March 2025**, marking the beginning of the transition phase.
- Most obligations start applying about **four years after entry into force**; some features may be adopted earlier by Member States on a voluntary basis.

## Implementation timeline (key milestones)

- **March 2025** — Regulation enters into force; transition period begins.
- **March 2027** — Deadline for the Commission to adopt several key implementing acts.
- **March 2029** — Key parts start to apply: primary-use exchange of the first group of priority categories (Patient Summaries, ePrescriptions/eDispensations) in all Member States; secondary-use rules start applying for most data categories (e.g. EHR data).
- **March 2031** — Second group of priority categories for primary use (medical images, lab results, hospital discharge reports) operational in all Member States; secondary-use rules apply to remaining categories (e.g. genomic data).
- **March 2035** — Third countries and international organisations may apply to join HealthData@EU for secondary use.

## Who benefits

- **Patients**: fast, free access to their own electronic health data; easy cross-border sharing with health professionals; more control (add information, restrict access, view access logs, request corrections); data in a standard European format (EEHRxF); privacy/security by default; opt-out rights from secondary use.
- **Health professionals**: faster access to patient records across providers and countries; reduced administrative burden.
- **Researchers**: access to large-scale health data; structured discovery of available data; more cost-efficient access to high-quality data.
- **Regulators/policymakers**: easier, transparent, cost-effective access for public-health monitoring and system efficiency.
- **Industry/innovators**: easier market access for EHR systems across Member States; greater availability of anonymised/pseudonymised data for research and innovation.

## Data protection and security

- Builds on GDPR, the Data Governance Act, the Data Act, and the NIS2 Directive, adding health-specific rules.
- Primary use: patients may restrict health-professional access to all or parts of their data exchanged through EHDS infrastructures; Member States may offer an opt-out for cross-border exchange.
- Secondary use: only for specific purposes set out in the Regulation, based on a permit issued by a **health data access body**; forbidden uses include decisions detrimental to individuals and marketing.
- Opt-out from secondary use is available in a simple, reversible manner (with limited public-interest exceptions under safeguards).
- Data processing for secondary use only in **secure processing environments**; no personal data can be downloaded; only pseudonymised data if anonymised is insufficient; re-identification is forbidden.
- Strict security and interoperability criteria for EHR systems, with manufacturer certification and a pre-/post-market compliance framework.
